A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same latent physics-emulation study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including the new Appendix D in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original autoencoder and emulation experiments on Euler, Rayleigh-Bénard and Turbulence Gravity Cooling, including ablations and guided rollouts.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction and emulation experiments and adds physical-distribution metrics and latent-representation analyses.

M1.justification: The overall autoencoder-plus-transformer framework remains. The stated reconstruction objective changes from L1 to field-averaged variance-normalized MSE, and Appendix B restricts conditioning masks to forward prediction, removing v1's reverse-mask sampling with probability 0.33. These revise training components without replacing the central approach.

E1.justification: The same three physical datasets and domains remain. Reported training coverage drops backward temporal prediction, while Appendix D adds a diagnostic task predicting Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers from latent tokens. The parameter-sensitivity experiments remain within existing fluid coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 14 substantially expands the reported comparator set with FNO, U-Net, PhysiX, TANTE, ViT+CSM and ViT+CKM. These are published results attributed to other studies, with differing settings, rather than newly controlled baseline runs. The original direct neural-solver comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds SEMD/Wasserstein evaluation and controlled parameter-sweep and probing protocols. RB horizons extend to 180 in Tables 6, 7 and 9, and Section 3.1 changes its stride from 4 to 1, although Table 2 still states 4. Table 3 also revises the 2D autoencoder size from 2.4e8 to 3.1e8 parameters. These establish substantial reported setting changes, but do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests Euler trajectory sensitivity to heat capacity at a fixed initial state and RB latent separability using an MLP, t-SNE and Bures-Wasserstein distances. Tables 11-13 add diagnostics of displacement and velocity/density distributions. The original optimizer/initialization ablation and context-length analysis remain, with some revised results.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the main evaluation with 64 test trajectories, 16 rollouts per case and the same spread-skill definitions. v2 introduces no training-seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests or new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: RB results are replaced across Tables 6, 7 and 9; for example, Table 6's diffusion model at compression 256 changes from 0.177 to 0.141 VRMSE over 1:20. These accompany revised reported settings, so they are not established same-setting gains. Table 7's TGC diffusion result for context 3 over 1:10 changes from 0.250 to 0.350. Tables 11-17 add substantial metric, comparison and latent-distance results.

T1.justification: The mathematical training objective changes, with v2 explicitly defining fieldwise VMSE in Appendix B, and the formal mask specification excludes reversed masks. The diffusion equations and Appendix A's spread-skill mathematics remain. The usable-information discussion adds no theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction and discussion narrow compression robustness specifically to diffusion-based emulation. The discussion now allows accuracy to improve with compression and qualifies the generative advantage as ensemble accuracy. The abstract and central compression, efficiency and generative-emulation contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds usable-information and iterative-sampling explanations and explicitly leaves theoretical explanation to future work. Appendix D interprets parameter separability as preserved physical distinctions. Table 14 adds a substantive qualification against claiming state-of-the-art performance across unequal settings. Existing fluid-domain and possible-overfitting limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B specifies VMSE field weighting and its 1e-2 stability constant; Table 3 revises parameter counts and removes the autoencoder attention-head specification. Appendix D documents compression choices, heat capacities and the central-token input for probing, but leaves probe-training details sparse. Code/weights disclosures and core hardware and training budgets remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to usable information, masked and flexible autoencoders, optimal transport and recent TheWell comparisons, alongside explicit non-state-of-the-art positioning. Some citations, including Zheng's masked-transformer training, Hairer's ODE text and Vaswani's attention paper, are removed. The main related-work narrative remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized methodology, results and discussion rewrites, clarifies conditioning notation, expands future-work explanations, updates acknowledgments and adds Appendix D. The title, abstract and main section sequence remain, without extensive document-wide restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 11-17 and Figures 22-23, changes plot palettes and captions, replaces RB image panels, and rearranges existing appendix figures and tables. Table 3's structure also changes. This substantially revises the visual presentation through both new displays and relocation of retained material.

improvement.justification: The physical-distribution metrics in Tables 11-13 and latent-space diagnostics in Appendix D provide more informative support than v1's existing accuracy and spectral evaluations alone. Narrower compression claims and Table 14's comparison caveat improve precision. These yield a modest net benefit, tempered by the newly conflicting RB stride statements and incomplete probe-training details.
